bench.machine: Apple host CPU; receipt/header metadata only
bench.rule: no hardware measurement claim without hardware

claim_boundary: Static sidecar artifact. No hardware measurement.

incomplete_in_the_specimens_directory.statement: these sit in specimens/ - the directory for COMPLETED downloads - with a parseable config and NO weight file at all. Directory placement is not evidence of completeness, and anything reading specimens/ as a done-list would have counted them.

lifecycle_is_derived_not_declared: SEALED_SOURCE requires a manifest with a resolved sha and byte count; FINGERPRINTED additionally requires config.json to parse and name an architecture; DOWNLOADING is a partial/ directory with no manifest. A specimen nothing supports is DISCOVERED, and that is not a claim anything is ready.

seal_backlog.not_every_check_is_equally_strong: INDEX_MATCHED compares the shard count to the specimen's own safetensors index. WEIGHTS_PRESENT_ONLY just says a weight file exists, which is what a non-safetensors layout allows. Sealing must verify bytes either way; this only says which are worth queueing first.
seal_backlog.statement: 29 specimens have complete weight shards matching their own index and no manifest, against 8 sealed. They are one verification pass from SEALED_SOURCE - NOT re-downloads - and until that pass runs they are invisible to a scheduler that acts only on sealed material.
seal_backlog.this_module_does_not_seal_them: sealing verifies bytes and writes a manifest, which is a ModelLake responsibility. A registry that sealed specimens as a side effect of being read would be a mutation writer pretending to be an observer.
seal_backlog.why_it_matters: S027 §2 assumes a newly sealed model becomes schedulable at once. The assumption holds; what is missing is that most of the library was never sealed, so the Odyssey's first cycle would see a small fraction of the specimens actually on disk.

shadowed_by_a_stale_partial_directory.reading: partial holds 305305 bytes against 96077777512 in specimens - under 1% - so it is a leftover fragment of a finished download, not a competing copy. It would still make a scheduler reading partial/ believe a download is in flight.

states_not_derivable_here.ACTIVE: a live scheduler state, not a disk fact
states_not_derivable_here.DISK_WARM: filesystem cache state is not observable from here
states_not_derivable_here.EVICTABLE: a residency decision, which is G104
states_not_derivable_here.EXECUTION_WARM: a live scheduler state, not a disk fact
states_not_derivable_here.LOADING: a live scheduler state, not a disk fact
states_not_derivable_here.NR_AVAILABLE: no NR index is written to the lake
states_not_derivable_here.NX_AVAILABLE: no NX index is written to the lake
states_not_derivable_here.PARKED: a live scheduler state, not a disk fact
states_not_derivable_here.UMA_RESIDENT: a live scheduler state, not a disk fact

what_this_does_not_do: it does not measure load cost, hold residency or choose what to load next - G102 and G104 own those. Every measured_load_seconds is null and says why, because a guessed load time is worse than an admitted unknown.
